ops.title: Driving the bluebubbles guest over VNC (vncdotool) — pointer is dropped, keyboard needs warm-up; the reliable recipe
ops.body:
Automating the bluebubbles guest's macOS Screen Sharing (`:5900` on its vmnet IP, ARD auth with the `yclaw-bluebubbles-admin-pass` admin creds) via `uvx --from vncdotool` has hard quirks. Learned 2026-07 bringing it onto the tailnet with no SSH/tailnet yet (VNC was the only channel).

**Pointer events are dropped entirely.** vncdotool `move`/`click` never register at any coordinate scale — Apple's Screen Sharing server ignores synthetic RFB pointer events. The cursor freezes wherever it was (often over the screen-sharing menubar icon, which is why the "Your screen is being controlled" popover sticks). Do NOT try to click, focus windows, or dismiss popovers with the mouse. Everything must be keyboard-only.

**Keyboard works but only after a warm-up.** A fresh vncdotool connection drops its first ~2-3s of keystrokes (a fixed "dead period" while the RFB handshake settles). Only PRINTABLE keys warm the path — modifier-only keys (shift) and special keys (arrows, return, backspace) do NOT warm it and get eaten during the dead period. Reliable recipe per connection: `time.sleep(1.5)` + one `captureScreen()` round-trip, then type ~30 throwaway `z` chars (0.08-0.1s apart) to absorb the dead period, THEN do real input. Persist ONE connection via `vncdotool.api.connect(server, password=PW, username="admin")` (ThreadedVNCClientProxy) — one-shot `vncdo` CLI invocations reset the dead period every time.

**Modifiers:** `super` = Command (NOT `meta`). Use the ATOMIC combo form `keyPress("super-space")` (Spotlight) — the manual `keyDown("super")/keyPress(k)/keyUp("super")` form is racy and mostly fails. Ctrl combos (`keyPress("ctrl-c")`, `ctrl-u`) proved unreliable even atomic; clear a line with a burst of plain `bsp` (backspace) keys instead (260 covers any accumulated length; past line-start is a harmless no-op). vncdotool `keyPress` splits on `-`, so a literal hyphen must be sent as `keyPress("minus")`; `esc` not `escape`; `return`/`enter` = 0xff0d.

**Getting a shell:** at the desktop, Finder is frontmost and clicks can't focus Terminal — launch/focus it with `super-space` → type `Terminal` → `return`. Then type commands into it. To submit a command reliably, do warm-up + clear + type + `return` all in ONE warm connection (a separate connection just to press Enter gets the Enter eaten). Verify the echoed command with a capture before it matters; a dropped trailing char is common, so end fragile commands with a valueless token (e.g. `--ssh`) so a truncation errors cleanly instead of corrupting an argument. NOTE: zsh interactive shells do NOT treat `#` as a comment (no `interactive_comments`), so `#pad` becomes a real argument — don't pad commands that way.

**Login screen:** one careful login only (lockout escalates — see [[metal-tailnet-recovery-2026-07]]). The password field scrolls/caps visible dots (~15) so you can't count 32; type from a verified-empty field (many `bsp` until the "Enter Password" placeholder returns) and submit with `return` in the same warm session.

Host→guest HTTP bootstrap (`curl … | bash` from the guest) does NOT work: the host's Application Firewall drops inbound to a Python `http.server` (connection reset/timeout). Type the command directly instead, embedding secrets via `echo "$PW" | sudo -S -p '' …`. See [[macos-guest-vm-ops]].
